title: Draft Commission Regulation amending Regulation (EU) 2017/2400 as regards adapting certain certification provisions for ensuring a uniform application of the determination of CO2 emissions and fuel consumption of medium and heavy lorries and heavy buses
description:
Commission Regulation (EU) 2017/2400 set outs the method for determining the CO2 emissions and fuel consumption of heavy-duty vehicles via the ‘VECTO’ software tool. The Regulation specifies provisions for testing vehicle components with an impact on CO2 emissions and fuel consumption that need to be provided as input to the software and sets outs requirements for manufacturers and Member States’ approval authorities to ensure the proper operation of the software. The resulting CO2 emission values are used to determine the average CO2 emissions per manufacturer. 

The proposed amendment to Regulation (EU) 2017/2400 aims to improve and clarify the existing testing and administrative provisions for the determination of CO₂ emissions from heavy-duty vehicles considering the increasing market uptake of vehicles with electric and hydrogen powertrains. Experience gained by manufacturers and approval authorities has identified areas requiring greater consistency, including component certification such as the air drag determination and reporting obligations.

The amendments are technical in nature and do not introduce new technologies or vehicle categories. They seek to ensure a uniform application of the Regulation and a level playing field among manufacturers, while providing additional flexibility for niche vehicle types and technologies not previously covered and facilitating CO₂ determination and reporting.

title: Proposal P1067 – Health Star Rating System: 2nd Call for Submissions and Supporting Documents (240 pages, in English).
description:
FSANZ has prepared a proposed draft amendment to the Australia New Zealand Food Standards Code (the Code) to mandate the display of a Health Star Rating (HSR) symbol on food for sale in Australia and New Zealand. The 2nd call for submissions provides FSANZ’s assessment and the proposed draft amendment, which would require the HSR to be calculated using a prescribed algorithm and the HSR symbol to be displayed on the front of most packaged foods for retail sale that are required to bear a nutrition information panel, subject to specified exemptions and prohibitions.  

FSANZ seeks submissions on the proposed regulatory approach to inform its final assessment and a decision on whether to approve, amend or reject the proposed draft amendment.
productsFreeText: Imported and domestically produced packaged foods for retail sale in Australia and New Zealand that are required to bear a label, subject to certain exemptions and prohibitions

objectives.name: Protection of human health or safety (TBT)

objectivesFreeText:
Diet plays an important role in overall health and wellbeing. Poor diet can contribute to overweight and obesity and increase the risk of diet-related non-communicable diseases. Around two-thirds of the Australian and New Zealand population are currently overweight or obese, and an estimated 15% of deaths in Australasia are attributable to dietary risks. National dietary guidelines emphasise the importance of choosing a variety of nutritious foods and limiting foods high in saturated fat, sugars and sodium.

 

The Health Star Rating (HSR) system is a front-of-pack nutrition labelling (FoPL) scheme that summarises a food’s overall nutritional profile using a simple star rating. Evidence indicates tools such as FoPL, used alongside other broader public health strategies, can improve consumer understanding of the healthfulness of foods and support healthier choices, with interpretive summary indicators like the HSR system generally performing favourably compared to other FoPL systems.

 

The objective of the HSR system is to provide a quick, easy, standardised way for consumers to compare the nutritional value of similar foods to help them make informed healthier food choices in-line with dietary guidelines.

 

Most consumers agree the HSR symbol makes it easier to identify healthier foods, and a majority report using the system at least sometimes when shopping. However, even though the system has been implemented on a voluntary basis for over 10 years, low uptake and selective use of the system by industry have limited effective consumer use.

The objective of this proposal is to consider requiring the HSR symbol on foods for sale in Australia and New Zealand to better support healthier food choices and thereby contribute to broader public health efforts to reduce the prevalence of overweight, obesity and diet-related non-communicable diseases in Australia and New Zealand.

title: Respirable Crystalline Silica and Respiratory Protection
description:
Proposed rule, request for comments; notice of public hearing - This proposed rule clarifies and modifies provisions of the respirable crystalline silica and respiratory protection standards that were established in the Mine Safety and Health Administration's (MSHA) 2024 final rule (notified as G/TBT/N/USA/2017/Add.3) titled ''Lowering Miners' Exposure to Respirable Crystalline Silica and Improving Respiratory Protection.'' The changes provide clarity and make improvements to the requirements for methods of compliance, exposure monitoring, respiratory protection, medical surveillance, and recordkeeping while maintaining strong protection of miners. The proposal also includes related conforming amendments.

 

MSHA will hold a virtual-only public hearing to provide industry, labor, and other interested parties with an opportunity to present oral statements, written comments, and other information on the proposed rule on 15 December 2026. If necessary, the hearing will continue on 16 December 2026. Pre-registration is not required to attend the hearing. Additional information on how to attend the virtual-only public hearing will be available at https://www.msha.gov/regulations/rulemaking/silica-public-hearing-information. Those who wish to speak during the virtual public hearing are encouraged to register in advance. Those who do not register in advance will have an opportunity to speak after all those who pre-registered have spoken.

title: Draft Commission Implementing Regulation amending Implementing Regulation (EU) 2022/1362 as regards the performance of heavy-duty trailers with e-axles, refrigeration units, solar systems or advanced aerodynamic devices with regard to their influence on the CO2 emissions, fuel consumption, energy consumption and zero emission driving range of motor vehicles
description:
Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2022/1362 establishes the methodology for determining the influence of heavy-duty trailers on the CO2 emissions, fuel consumption, energy consumption and zero-emission driving range of motor vehicles by means of a simulation tool. It lays down requirements for the operation of the simulation tool and for determining the characteristics of trailer components and systems that serve as inputs to the tool.

The proposed amendment updates this methodology to reflect technological developments and technologies that have become available or reached sufficient technological maturity since the adoption of Regulation (EU) 2022/1362. In particular, it introduces provisions for electrified trailer axles, electrified refrigeration systems, solar energy systems and advanced aerodynamic devices, and extends the relevant input data and models used by the simulation tool. It also introduces specific provisions for refrigerated trailers and semi-trailers, including those with volume-oriented configurations, and provides for the monitoring of vehicles that are currently not capable of being simulated. 

The amendment also aims to reduce duplication of testing and certification and the associated administrative burden by allowing, where appropriate, certified values established under Regulation (EU) 2017/2400 to be used as inputs to the trailer simulation tool. In addition, it introduces provisions facilitating the certification and use of combinations of aerodynamic devices and provides greater flexibility in determining the performance of vehicles equipped with technologies not previously covered by the methodology.

title: Framework for managing sustainable development in business districts
description:
IWA 9:2011 provides a framework for managing sustainable development in a business district, including the evaluation, comparison and improvement of its performance. It also identifies and describes factors to be considered when developing and evaluating the economic, environmental and social performance of new and existing business districts.

IWA 9:2011 can also be used to compare or assess the performance of business districts regarding the provisions described within it.

IWA 9:2011 does not set benchmarks or expected levels of performance regarding the impacts of business districts.

IWA 9:2011 is intended to be used in conjunction with, and in accordance with the principles set out in, ISO 15392, ISO 26000 and the standards on environmental management prepared by ISO/TC 207.

title: Modification of Significant New Use Rules of Certain Chemical Substances (23-1.M)
description:
The Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) is amending significant new use rules (SNURs) issued under section 5(a)(2) of the Toxic Substances Control Act (TSCA) for certain chemical substances identified herein, which were the subject of premanufacture notices (PMNs) and significant new use notices (SNUNs). This action amends the SNURs by allowing certain new uses reported in the SNUNs or PMNs without additional notification requirements, modifying the significant new use notification requirements based on the actions and determinations for the SNUN or PMN submissions or based on the examination of new test data or other information, and making technical amendments to several SNURs. EPA is issuing these amendments based on review of new and existing data for the chemical substances.

 

This rule is effective on 11 January 2027. For purposes of judicial review, this rule shall be promulgated at 1 p.m. Eastern Standard Time (EST) on 24 November 2026.

title: Revisions of the Notification of the Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry (METI) under the Act on the Rational Use of Energy
description:
Under the Act on the Rational Use of Energy (Law No. 49 of 1979; hereinafter referred to as the “Energy Efficiency Law”), the Minister of Economy, Trade and Industry shall establish and publicize standards for manufacturers/importers (hereinafter referred to as the “manufacturers, etc.”), with regard to the improvement of the energy efficiency performance of each type of equipment specified by Cabinet Order under the Energy Efficiency Law, including gas or oil water heaters. 

The Minister shall also specify the information to be displayed by manufacturers, etc., with regard to the energy efficiency of the specified equipment, including gas or oil water heaters. 

In addition, the energy efficiency standards shall be established taking into consideration the highest level of energy consumption performance of the respective types of specified equipment and other related factors.

Since the water heating sector accounts for around 30% of energy consumption in residential properties, it is the largest end-use of energy in households. To further promote energy efficiency in this sector, the Minister proposes new energy efficiency standards for gas water heaters.

title: Resolution of the Cabinet of Ministries of Ukraine of 28 October 2026 No. 1333 “On Amendments to Certain Resolutions of the Cabinet of Ministers of Ukraine Concerning the Introduction of Electronic Traceability of the Circulation of Alcoholic Beverages, Tobacco Products and Liquids Used in Electronic Cigarettes” and Resolution of the Cabinet of Ministries of Ukraine of 28 October 2026 No. 1334 “On Amendments to Certain Resolutions of the Cabinet of Ministers of Ukraine Concerning the Postponement of the Dates for Putting into Operation the Electronic System for the Circulation of Alcoholic Beverages, Tobacco Products and Liquids Used in Electronic Cigarettes”
description:
Ukraine notifies the adoption of Resolutions of the Cabinet of Ministers of Ukraine No. 1333 and No. 1334 of 28 October 2026, which amend the regulatory framework governing the electronic marking and traceability of alcoholic beverages, tobacco products and liquids used in electronic cigarettes.

In particular, Resolution No. 1333 postpones the implementation of certain provisions concerning the electronic marking of these products and the use of unique identifiers from 1 November 2026 to 1 July 2027. It also postpones the repeal of certain previous regulatory acts from 1 May 2027 to 1 January 2028.

Resolution No. 1334 extends the testing period of the Electronic System until 30 June 2027. It provides that, from 1 January to 30 June 2027, the System will operate in test mode, taking into account the specific transitional arrangements established by the Resolution. Full operation of the System is scheduled to commence on 1 July 2027.

The Resolution also provides for the retention of information entered into the System during the transitional period and exempts economic operators registered in the System between 1 January and 30 June 2027 from repeated registration as of 1 July 2027.

The amendments are intended to provide additional time for testing and preparation for the full implementation of the Electronic System.

description: The notified interministerial order amends two orders by setting a timetable for reducing the maximum permissible cadmium content in certain fertilizers and growing media, and the maximum permissible amounts of cadmium when using fertilizers.It applies to fertilizers and growing media placed on the market and used under the conditions provided for in Articles L. 255-2 to L. 255-4 and paragraphs 1, 3 and 5 of Article L. 255-5 of the Rural and Maritime Fishing Code.Unless a measure is adopted pursuant to Article 114(5) of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union, this Order shall not apply to fertilizing substances and growing G/TBT/N/FRA/246- 2 - media placed on the market and used in accordance with the conditions laid down in Article L 255-5, i.e. fertilizers complying with Regulation (EU) 2019/1009.The two amended orders are:Order of 18 September 2026 establishing the assessment procedures and values for the safety and end-of-waste criteria for fertilizers and growing media; andOrder of 18 September 2026 establishing the maximum acceptable amounts of trace metal elements and trace organic compounds when using fertilizers.
